newsitem.title: SPAIN: SPAIN SAYS ARBED TO RAISE CSI PRODUCTIVITY.
newsitem.headline: SPAIN SAYS ARBED TO RAISE CSI PRODUCTIVITY.

text.p: State holding firm AIE said on Tuesday it chose Luxembourg steel maker Arbed as a strategic partner for Spanish steel company Corporacion Siderurgica Integral (CSI) because of its plans to increase productivity at the Spanish firm.
"Arbed's plan is on the one hand to strengthen the management of the firm, and on the other to improve productivity," said AIE's chairman Fernando Prada, speaking at a press conference.

CSI will increase capital by 129.0 billion pesetas, with Arbed subscribing the whole issue for a 35 percent stake in the state-owned steel firm. CSI will then invest some 100 billion pesetas of that amount in stakes in Arbed group companies.

The government, which received two competing offers for the group, overcame objections to a deal by worried workers who have held a series of short strikes this month amid concern jobs would be lost in a sale.
The deal reached includes the maintenance of present jobs, although any normal retirements will go ahead. Thus staff will total 11,266 in 2001 versus 11,624 at present.
Arbed is also committed to maintaining current installations, and may not modify its 35 percent stake.
In the case of a hostile takeover bid, agreement with trades unions, or authorisation by the government, Arbed may issue warrants with rights to increase capital by 15 percent.

Under the terms of the Arbed deal, CSI will buy a 9.5 percent stake in Arbed for 36.4 billion pesetas, and will also buy 25 percent stakes in Sidstahl and Europrofil. The price of the latter two stakes was not specified.
CSI will also buy other Arbed participations for 40.3 billion pesetas.
Arbed will invest 156.0 billion pesetas in CSI in the next five years, versus an initial plan by AIE to invest 86.0 billion, Prada added.
"The entry of Arbed will mean an around 30 billion peseta improvement in CSI's cash position," Prada said.
After the capital increase CSI's equity will stand at 369.2 billion pesetas.
"The resulting group will be the biggest European iron and steel group and the third biggest in the world," he added.
The government plans to float between 51 and 65 percent of CSI on the stock exchange this year, market conditions permitting.
According to a report drawn up by AIE, the Spanish steel firm, once privatised, has sufficient funds to guarantee a "very reasonable" dividend in the next few years.
